original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: On the 112 live lines of the pinned coordinate-frame complement, does low_weight_words return exactly the weight-at-most-16 words of the 36-dimensional F2 incidence code of the 1260 orthogonal 8-frames?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a new measured speedup. The revision-8 verification row says a published faster replay is not equivalent coverage until checked. The merged E7 comparison and the E6 4-frame comparison already bound two codes. This package answers the P112 half of the question those comparisons left open. It does not time an engine or install one.
bottleneck_link: Deletion and decoder certificates reuse this iterator only if another code still returns every low-weight word. This comparison binds that iterator to one P112 punctured frame code. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after one P112 incidence code, two half-splits of its kernel, and one engine batch. Do not remeasure timings, rerun the E6 or D6 census, or load the intersection-counter engine.
evidence: The incidence matrix of 1260 orthogonal 8-frames on the 112 live lines has F2 rank 76 and kernel dimension 36, with the recorded free coordinates. Half-splits after 18 and after 16 generators agree on all 2^36 weights. The only words of weight at most 16 are zero and seven disjoint weight-16 blocks, which are the three cross-pair matchings and the four even spinor pairs of the coordinate frame. low_weight_words at batch size 20 returns that set. A moved block, a weight-15 injection, a dropped support, and a repeated generator fail.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does one reflected copy of this coordinate frame induce the same set equality after the root list is transported?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This pin is one orthogonal 8-frame. A second frame is a different ordered basis even if the parameters match.
open_questions.first_step: Reflect one punctured root by one simple E8 root, rebuild the 112-line list, and compare one half-split with the transported images of these seven supports.
open_questions.blocked_by: No second frame is pinned in this package.

open_questions.question: Does the opt-in intersection-counter engine return this same 8-word set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A faster substitute is not coverage for this basis until the sets are compared. This is not the E6 64-word hash and not the D6 16-word set.
open_questions.first_step: Run research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py on this 36-generator basis at one batch size and compare it with the support hash recorded here.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not load that engine.
